name: cap-document-validation-use
description: How to use document validation as a caller: send the document and the name of the shape it claims to be, get back admitted or a located list of everything wrong. Covers the three ways in - a person, an agent, an event - the minimal inputs and outputs, two worked examples, and the failure body you will actually receive. Load it when you are submitting anything to this platform, when a submission came back rejected and you are deciding what to fix, when you are about to hand-write field checks in your own component, and when someone asks 'what exactly do I have to send', 'why was this refused', or 'if we tighten the rules, what breaks for callers'.

purpose.text: Make the capability usable in two moves - send a document with the name of its shape, read a located list back - so a caller never has to know which validator, dialect or schema store served the call.

operations.name: validate, as a caller sees it (proposed view of the operation cap-document-validation defines)
operations.input: two things: the document you are submitting, and the identifier of the shape it claims to be (proposed)
operations.output: admitted, or a list of every violation with the location of each inside your document (proposed)

shapes.name: worked example 1 (proposed): a person submits a malformed entry and gets everything wrong with it, at once

examples.what_the_caller_does: fixes both violations in one edit and resubmits; there is no second round of discovery

shapes.name: worked example 2 (proposed): the shape is tightened and no caller changes

schema.title: Enhancing one aspect without touching the rest (proposed)

examples.change: the schema adds a maxLength and a pattern to idempotency_key; the schema id gains a new version
unchanged: what a caller sends: the same document and the same shape identifier
the outcome shape they read back
every other schema in the store

newly_rejected.message: does not match the required pattern

examples.who_had_to_change: nobody's calling code; only the schema resource and the callers whose documents were already out of shape

invariants.text: All three ways in reach the same check: a person, an agent, and an internal or external event submit through one envelope, against one shape identifier, and read one outcome shape back.
invariants.quote: All four enter through the same shape

invariants.text: A caller supplies two things and knows nothing else: the document, and the identifier of the shape it claims to be. Which validator ran, which dialect it resolved and where the schema lives are all hidden.

Tightening a schema, replacing the validator behind the interface, and changing how a rejection is rendered are three independent changes; none of them alters what a caller sends or the outcome shape they read.
invariants.quote: Composability allows enhancing particular aspects of any element without touching the rest.

invariants.text: A rejection arrives as data: a located list of every violation, carried on the wire as problem details with a type, title, status and detail. Match on the type; never parse the wording.
invariants.quote: A Problem Details response uses the application/problem+json content type

invariants.text: cap-document-validation already states the well-formedness finding for this capability (F-a7-03). For a caller it means admitted says your document is shaped correctly, and says nothing about whether what you asked for is sensible or affordable.

not_exposed.text: Proposed: cap-document-validation lists what this interface hides. The practical form for a caller is that no answer you receive names a library, a file path, a process or a version - so if you find yourself branching on one, you are reading something you were not given.

instructions.action: Send the document together with the identifier of the shape it claims to be, through the same envelope whether you are a person typing it, an agent submitting it, or an event carrying it.
instructions.why: All three must be able to enter, and one entry shape is what lets the same check, the same outcome and the same record apply to all of them.
instructions.quote: An internal or external event must be able to enter the system.

instructions.action: Read the outcome as data. On rejection, work through the whole located list and fix it in one edit; do not stop at the first entry and do not pattern-match the message text.
instructions.why: Every violation is reported in one pass precisely so that repair is one round rather than as many rounds as your document has faults.
instructions.quote: All errors are reported in a single pass instead of stopping at the first failure.

instructions.action: On the wire, expect problem details: branch on the type field, read status for the class of failure, and show detail to a person rather than to your code.
instructions.why: A typed body is the difference between a caller that keeps working when the wording improves and one that breaks on a copy edit.

instructions.action: When you need a stricter rule, tighten the schema and publish it under a new identifier; do not add a check in your own component and do not ask callers to change what they send.
instructions.why: The shape is the one place a rule can change without reaching anyone: worked example 2 is that change written out.
instructions.quote: Composability allows enhancing particular aspects of any element without touching the rest.

instructions.action: Do not re-check the document after admission with hand-written field tests of your own.
instructions.why: Proposed: two checkers give two answers, and the second one is the one nobody maintains; it is also how a rule ends up enforced on one entry path and not the others.

instructions.action: If a result surprises you, ask which dialect was in effect for the call rather than reading the schema file and reasoning from it.
instructions.why: cap-document-validation already states why (F-a7-04): what a file declares and what a runtime resolved are different facts, and only one of them decided your outcome.
instructions.quote: Values written to YAML validated, reviewed correctly, and had no runtime effect

instructions.action: If you cannot state the shape you must send in a sentence, say so and treat it as a defect in the schema rather than working around it.
instructions.why: A shape a caller cannot hold in their head gets guessed at instead, and a capability nobody can use straightforwardly is one nobody uses.
instructions.quote: It cannot be daunting or overly complex, or no one will use it.

best_practices.text: Ask for every violation at once with the location of each, rather than a first-failure answer; it is the difference between one repair and one repair per fault.
best_practices.quote: return all validation errors at once with field-level detail

best_practices.text: Proposed: version the shape, never the caller. Publishing a new schema identifier lets old and new documents coexist while they migrate; adding an optional field with special meaning to an existing shape makes every reader guess which era a document came from.

Proposed: validate the envelope once, at the way in, and let composition carry the result; a step that revalidates the same document is paying for the check twice and can still disagree with the admission point.
Keep what a caller must know small: two inputs and one outcome. Every additional thing a caller must configure is a reason the check gets bypassed rather than used.
best_practices.quote: It has to be simple to use.

definition_of_done.criterion: Proposed tool, built with the entry seam: `python3 tools/use_check_document_validation.py --entry human --entry event --entry external --schema urn:agentic:seam:entry:0.1 --valid fixtures/entry/valid.json --malformed fixtures/entry/malformed.json`. It asserts that the valid instance is admitted through all three entries with byte-identical outcomes, that the malformed instance is rejected through all three with the same problem type `urn:agentic:problem:document-invalid`, media type `application/problem+json` and the same located error list, and that `entries_run == 3` and `errors_reported > 1`.
definition_of_done.expected: exit 0 and the line `entries_run=3 identical_outcomes=1 problem_type=urn:agentic:problem:document-invalid errors_reported=2`.
definition_of_done.breakage: Have one entry path stamp a default field into the document before it is validated - for example a priority the other two entries do not set.
definition_of_done.expected_failure: That entry's outcome diverges from the other two, `identical_outcomes=0`, the run names which entry differed, and it exits non-zero while the other two entries still agree - so the check says which way in broke the equivalence rather than only that it broke.
definition_of_done.quote: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion

open_questions.question: Should a caller be able to validate a document without submitting it - a dry run against a shape?
open_questions.evidence: Count, over recorded submissions, how many were rejected for shape alone and how many of those came from an agent that could have checked first; if that fraction is large, the pre-check pays for itself in refused work.
open_questions.default: Yes, using the same operation and the same outcome, with nothing dispatched and nothing spent. Proposed: it costs one call path and removes the reason an agent would keep a private copy of the rules.
